mainTopic: Animals forbidden for the מזבח: why they are never cancelled in a mixture, why our משנה is needed, and the source that רובע and נרבע are unfit.
overview: The משנה lists animals that may never be brought on the מזבח, such as רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טרפה and יוצא דופן. If one of them gets mixed in with good animals, the whole group is forbidden for the מזבח, no matter how small its share. The משנה also defines מוקצה and נעבד and says both may still be eaten. The גמרא explains that these animals are never cancelled by a majority, then asks why our משנה is needed when משניות in זבחים and עבודה זרה seem to teach the same thing. Through a chain of answers (צריכותא), it shows that each משנה teaches something new: our משנה covers animals that are only unfit for the מזבח and that got mixed while still חולין. Next the גמרא asks for the source that רובע and נרבע are unfit, and brings a ברייתא that learns it from the words מן הבהמה. The ברייתא tests whether a קל וחומר could teach this instead, and finds that it works only when two witnesses saw the sin. רבי שמעון offers a קל וחומר for the one-witness case too, and the גמרא explains that the רבנן who disagree with him still need the פסוק.

steps.title: Forbidden altar animals make a whole mixture forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that animals forbidden for the מזבח make any mixture forbidden in any amount. It then lists which animals these are.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Every animal that is forbidden to be offered on the מזבח makes the whole mixture forbidden, however small its share. These are: an animal that mated with a person, an animal a person mated with, the set-aside animal, the worshipped animal, the prostitute's payment, the price of a dog, the crossbred animal, the טרפה, and the animal born by caesarean section.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new topic. If an animal that can't go on the מזבח gets mixed in with good animals, none of them can be brought, no matter how many good ones there are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small forbidden item can get 'lost' in a large permitted majority. The משנה says that does not happen here: 'בכל שהן' means even a tiny share forbids everything. It then lists nine kinds of animals that fall under this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core text the גמרא will discuss)
In any amount at all, even a tiny share
An animal that mated with a person / that a person mated with
An animal given as payment to a prostitute / given in exchange for a dog
An animal with a fatal defect
An animal born through the side (caesarean section)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'בכל שהן' is the main topic of the גמרא that follows. The גמרא will ask why this משנה is needed at all.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All animals that are forbidden for the altar
make [a mixture] forbidden in any amount
phrases.notes: The case is when one of these got mixed into a group of good animals. Even one makes them all unusable for the altar.

phrases.english: the animal that mated with a person, and the animal a person mated with
and the set-aside animal, and the worshipped animal
and the prostitute's payment, and the price [of a dog]
and the crossbred animal, and the tereifa
and the animal born by caesarean section

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הָאֲסוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ אוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals forbidden for the מזבח are not cancelled in a mixture. Even a tiny share makes the whole mixture forbidden for offering.

steps.title: Defining the set-aside and the worshipped animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what מוקצה and נעבד are and how they differ for the items on the animal. It adds that both may still be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a set-aside animal? One set aside for idol worship. The animal itself is forbidden, but what is on it is permitted. What is a worshipped animal? Any animal people worship. The animal and what is on it are both forbidden. Both of these may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines two items from its list. מוקצה is an animal set aside to be used for idol worship. נעבד is an animal that people actually worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מוקצה, only the animal is banned from the מזבח; its decorations may be sold to buy a קרבן. With נעבד, even its decorations are banned. Still, both kinds of animal may be eaten as ordinary food, because an animal does not become forbidden to eat just because it was worshipped.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside for idol worship
An animal that is itself worshipped as an idol
What is on it (its decorations or coverings)
Permitted to be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden' here means forbidden for the מזבח, not forbidden to eat. The משנה says clearly that both animals may be eaten.

phrases.english: Which is the set-aside animal?
One that is set aside for idol worship
it is forbidden, but what is on it is permitted
And which is the worshipped animal?
Any animal that people worship
it and what is on it are forbidden
And both this one and that one are permitted to be eaten

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines two of the terms in the list from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוקצה: only the animal is banned from the מזבח. נעבד: the animal and its decorations are banned. Both may be eaten.

steps.title: In any amount means no cancelling by majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'בכל שהן': these animals are not cancelled out by a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Master said: 'They make a mixture forbidden in any amount.' This means they are not cancelled out by a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase and explains its meaning. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the rule of ביטול ברוב lets a minority become 'part of' the majority. The גמרא says the משנה is teaching that this rule does not apply to animals forbidden for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Are cancelled out by a majority (ביטול ברוב)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Master said
"They make [a mixture] forbidden in any amount"
meaning that they are not cancelled by a majority

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening rule of the משנה in step 1 to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals forbidden for the מזבח are not cancelled by ביטול ברוב.

steps.title: We already learned this in another משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a משנה in זבחים already teaches that קדשים mixed with forbidden animals are not cancelled, even one in ten thousand. So why repeat it here?
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this: all sacrificial animals that got mixed with sin offerings left to die, or with an ox sentenced to stoning, even one in ten thousand, must all be left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה as repeating something already taught. A משנה in זבחים already said that a forbidden animal in a mixture is never cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In זבחים, a חטאת that must be left to die or a שור הנסקל gets mixed with קדשים, and the whole group must die. That already shows forbidden animals are not cancelled by a majority. So what does our משנה add?

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings that must be left to die
An ox sentenced to be stoned (forbidden for any benefit)
One in ten thousand

phrases.english: We have already learned this
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in זבחים 70b.

phrases.english: All sacrificial animals that got mixed
with sin offerings that are left to die
or with an ox sentenced to stoning
even one in ten thousand
they must [all] be left to die

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation in step 3 as already taught elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for our משנה's rule of 'בכל שהן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in זבחים already teaches that forbidden animals in a mixture are not cancelled even one in ten thousand. So our משנה seems to repeat it.

steps.title: The wording 'even' in that משנה was puzzling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that the wording of the משנה in זבחים was already hard for them to understand: what is it saying?
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was difficult for us: what is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up an older difficulty with the wording of the משנה in זבחים. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain that משנה and use it to answer the question about our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even one in ten thousand' sounds like the easy case: one good animal among ten thousand forbidden ones. The real big news would be the opposite case, one forbidden animal among many good ones. So the word 'even' seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for us
What is it saying?

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not answering the challenge yet. It only points to a problem in the wording of the משנה in זבחים. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: And it was difficult for us
what is it saying?
phrases.notes: The puzzle is the word 'even.' One good animal among ten thousand forbidden ones is the easier case, so why say 'even'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a wording problem in the source quoted in step 4. This prepares the answer to that challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'even' in 'even one in ten thousand' in the משנה in זבחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a forbidden minority already forbids a mixture, then a forbidden majority obviously does. So 'even' seems to introduce the weaker case.

steps.title: How to read the משנה in זבחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the wording of the משנה in זבחים: if forbidden animals like חטאות המתות or a שור הנסקל get mixed in with offerings, all of them must die, even if it is one in ten thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if some of the sin offerings that are left to die, or an ox that is to be stoned, got mixed in with them, then even one in ten thousand, they must all die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from step 5 by explaining what the משנה in זבחים is really saying. This sets up the main question again: if זבחים already teaches this, why does our משנה repeat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in זבחים is about animals that are forbidden for any benefit at all: חטאות המתות and a שור הנסקל. When one of these is mixed into a group of offerings, the whole group is forbidden and must die, no matter how small the forbidden part is. Once this reading is clear, the overlap with our משנה stands out.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching. The גמרא uses this to explain the real meaning of a hard-to-read source.
The five kinds of sin offerings that cannot be brought and are left to die.
An ox sentenced to be stoned, for example because it killed a person. No one may benefit from it.
Ten thousand.

phrases.english: This is what it is teaching:
If there were mixed in with them some of the sin offerings that are left to die,
phrases.notes: 'With them' means mixed in with offerings that are fine for the מזבח.

phrases.english: or an ox that is to be stoned,
even one in ten thousand, they must all die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording difficulty raised in step 5, and this brings back the question from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording of the משנה in זבחים was unclear.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means that offerings mixed with חטאות המתות or a שור הנסקל must all die, even one in ten thousand.

steps.title: Our משנה is needed for animals that are not forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה is still needed. זבחים deals with animals forbidden for any benefit. Our animals are only forbidden for the מזבח, so we might have thought they are cancelled by the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: only there, where the animals are forbidden for any benefit, is the mixture forbidden. But here, where they are not forbidden for benefit, I would say they are cancelled by the majority. So the משנה teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4 about why our משנה repeats a rule from זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are not the same. חטאות המתות and a שור הנסקל are forbidden for any benefit, which is a very strict ban. Our animals, like מוקצה and נעבד, may still be eaten and used and are only forbidden as offerings. So we might have thought a weaker ban gets cancelled by the majority, and our משנה teaches that even these are never cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed. The גמרא's standard answer when asked why a source is repeated.
It would have entered your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought.
Things that are forbidden for any benefit at all, not just for eating.
Cancelled by the majority. A forbidden item that is lost in a larger permitted mixture is treated as gone.
So it teaches us. This introduces the new point a source is making.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even an animal forbidden only as an offering, and not for benefit, makes a mixture forbidden in any amount.

phrases.english: It was needed,
because it would have entered your mind to say:
It is only there, since they are forbidden for any benefit,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in זבחים about חטאות המתות and a שור הנסקל.

phrases.english: but here, where they are not forbidden for benefit,
I would say: let them be cancelled by the majority.
So it teaches us that they are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition question from step 4, now that step 6 has made the זבחים case clear.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only animals forbidden for any benefit make a mixture forbidden. Animals forbidden only as offerings are cancelled by the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even animals forbidden only for the מזבח are never cancelled, so our משנה adds something new.

steps.title: זבחים already teaches about רובע and נרבע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה in זבחים also teaches about רובע and נרבע, which are not forbidden for benefit. There the rule is that the mixed animals must graze until they get a blemish and then be sold. So זבחים already covers our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we also already learned about רובע and נרבע: if a רובע or a נרבע got mixed in, they should graze until they get a blemish and then be sold, and the owner brings an offering of that same kind, worth as much as the best animal among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 7 by quoting another part of the משנה in זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said זבחים only taught about animals forbidden for benefit. But זבחים also deals with רובע and נרבע, which are only forbidden for the מזבח, and it still treats the whole mixture as unfit to offer. So the חידוש that step 7 gave our משנה is already in זבחים, and the repetition question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that had relations with a person.
An animal that a person had relations with.
They should graze until they get a blemish, so that they lose their holiness and can be sold.
The best among them. The new offering must be worth as much as the most valuable animal in the mixture.

steps.confusionAlert: Being sold does not mean the mixture became permitted for the מזבח. None of the mixed animals may be offered; they are sold only once they have a blemish.

phrases.english: But we also already learned about an animal that lay with a person and one that a person lay with:
If a רובע or a נרבע got mixed in with offerings,
they should graze until they get a blemish, and then be sold,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵי יָפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין!
phrases.english: and he brings, with money equal to the best of them, an offering of that same kind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that זבחים teaches only about animals forbidden for any benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: זבחים also rules on רובע and נרבע, which are not forbidden for benefit, so our משנה still seems to repeat it.

steps.title: One משנה is about חולין, the other about קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב שימי בר אשי answered: one משנה is about animals that got mixed while still חולין, and the other is about animals mixed when already קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I said this teaching before רב שימי בר אשי, and he said to me: one is about animals that are חולין, and the other is about animals that are קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to why both משניות are needed, quoting רב שימי בר אשי through רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two משניות are about different moments of mixing. The משנה in זבחים opens with 'all the offerings', so it is about animals that were already holy when they got mixed. Our משנה is about animals that got mixed while still חולין and were made holy afterward, so it teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling. Here it means this difficulty and its discussion.
Ordinary animals that are not holy.
Holy animals that are already set aside as offerings.

steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות are needed. זבחים is about animals already holy when they got mixed. Our משנה is about animals mixed while still חולין and made holy afterward. Either way, animals forbidden for the מזבח are never cancelled by the majority.

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: I said this teaching before רב שימי בר אשי,
and he said to me: one is about animals that are חולין,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה: the animals got mixed while ordinary, and the owner made them holy later.

phrases.english: and the other is about animals that are קדשים.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in זבחים, which opens with 'all the offerings', so they were already holy when mixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 with a new way of telling the two משניות apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each משנה is about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to teach the same rule about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: זבחים is about animals mixed when already holy. Our משנה is about animals mixed while still חולין and made holy later.

steps.title: Why both the קדשים case and the חולין case are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we need both משניות. From the קדשים case alone, we might have said the animals are forbidden only because they became disgusting to the מזבח. In the חולין case we might have said they are cancelled by the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If we had only been taught the case of קדשים, we would say the reason is that they are disgusting to the מזבח. But with חולין, we would say: let them be cancelled by the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב שימי בר אשי's answer by showing that each משנה teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals mixed after they were already קדשים are pushed away from the מזבח at once, because they have become 'disgusting' to it. Animals mixed while still חולין were never pushed away, so we might think the forbidden one is simply cancelled by the majority. Our משנה teaches that the whole mixture is forbidden even then.

keyTerms.meaning: They are both needed. Each source teaches something the other does not.
They are disgusting, meaning rejected as unfit for the מזבח
Let them be cancelled, meaning the forbidden one is lost in the majority (ביטול ברוב)
Ordinary animals that have not been set aside as offerings

phrases.english: And both are needed, for if it had taught us only about sacred animals,
that would be because they are disgusting to the altar,
but regarding non-sacred animals, I would say: let them be cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 9 by explaining why each משנה is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches a case the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals mixed while still חולין are never disgusting to the מזבח, so the forbidden one would be cancelled by the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even animals mixed while still חולין make the whole mixture forbidden for the מזבח.

steps.title: A משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches mixtures of non-sacred items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we already learned in עבודה זרה that certain forbidden things forbid a whole mixture in any amount, even in a non-sacred setting. So why do we need our משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we also learned this about non-sacred things: These are forbidden, and they make a mixture forbidden in any amount: wine poured for idols, an idol, the birds of a מצורע, and hides torn at the heart. Also the hair of a נזיר, a firstborn donkey, meat cooked in milk, an ox that is to be stoned, the עגלה ערופה, non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, and the scapegoat. These are forbidden and make a mixture forbidden in any amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה listing forbidden things that forbid any mixture they fall into. It argues that this already covers the non-sacred case our משנה teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said our משנה is needed for the חולין case. The גמרא now points out that the משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches about non-sacred mixtures, and its rule is very strict: even a tiny amount forbids everything. If so, our משנה seems to add nothing again.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden themselves, and they also make other things they mix with forbidden
In any amount at all. Even one in a huge mixture is not cancelled.
Wine poured as an offering to an idol
Animal hides with a tear at the heart, a sign the animal was used for idol worship
Ordinary animals slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard, which become forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Some items on this list are holy items (like the נזיר's hair), but none of them is an offering mixed in with offerings for the מזבח. The גמרא brings this משנה because it teaches the rule for ordinary mixtures.

phrases.english: But about non-sacred things we also learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in עבודה זרה 74a.

phrases.english: And these are forbidden, and they forbid a mixture in any amount:
wine poured for idols, and an idol,
and the birds of a leper, and hides torn at the heart.
And the hair of a nazirite, and a firstborn donkey,
and meat cooked in milk, and an ox that is to be stoned,
and the heifer whose neck is broken, and non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard,
and the scapegoat:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאוֹסְרִין בְּכׇל שֶׁהֵן!
phrases.english: these are forbidden, and they forbid a mixture in any amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 10 by showing that another משנה already covers non-sacred mixtures.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה is needed to teach the rule for animals mixed while still חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches that forbidden things in non-sacred mixtures forbid the whole mixture in any amount, so our משנה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: עבודה זרה deals with items forbidden for all benefit; ours does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both are still needed. The עבודה זרה list is about things forbidden for any benefit, which are never cancelled. Our animals are only unfit for the מזבח, so we might have thought they are cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it had taught us only there, we would say that is because they are forbidden for any benefit, so they are not cancelled. But here, let them be cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends our משנה by showing that the עבודה זרה case is stricter than ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on the עבודה זרה list is forbidden for any benefit, and such items are not cancelled in a mixture. Our animals, such as מוקצה and נעבד (which the משנה says may be eaten), are only unfit for the מזבח, so we might have thought the majority cancels them. Our משנה teaches that even these make the whole mixture forbidden for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Things you may not get any benefit or use from at all
They are cancelled, meaning lost in the majority of a mixture
There, the other משנה / here, our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה adds a new rule. Even animals that are only unfit for the מזבח, and that got mixed while still חולין, are not cancelled by the majority. The whole mixture is forbidden for the מזבח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a mixture can stay forbidden even when the forbidden item is not forbidden for benefit, if the issue is fitness for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Both are needed, for if it had taught us only there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה in עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: that is because they are forbidden for any benefit, so they are not cancelled,
but here, let them be cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by pointing to a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: telling the cases apart by type of prohibition (forbidden for all benefit vs. only unfit for the מזבח)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals only unfit for the מזבח, and not forbidden for benefit, would be cancelled by the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even such animals make the whole mixture forbidden for the מזבח, so our משנה is needed.

steps.title: Why the עבודה זרה list is still needed
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the answer from Step 12. If we only had our משנה, we might think the animals forbid the mixture only because they are disgusting to the מזבח, while things forbidden for benefit could be cancelled by a majority. The משנה in עבודה זרה teaches that they are not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תנא had taught this only here, I would say the mixture is forbidden because these animals are disgusting for the מזבח. But for regular people, I would say that things forbidden for benefit should be cancelled by a majority. So the משנה in עבודה זרה teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows that our משנה alone would not teach us what the עבודה זרה משנה teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed why our משנה is needed even though we have the עבודה זרה list. Now the גמרא shows the other side. A rule that is only about the מזבח could be explained by the idea that the animal is disgusting to Heaven, and that idea would not carry over to ordinary use. So we need the עבודה זרה משנה to teach that איסורי הנאה are not cancelled in a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The Most High, meaning the מזבח and offerings to ה׳
Disgusting or repulsive
An ordinary person; regular, non-sacred use
Things you may not get any benefit from
Cancelled by a majority
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: Each משנה teaches something the other cannot. Our משנה shows that animals unfit for the מזבח are not cancelled in a mixture. The עבודה זרה משנה shows that איסורי הנאה are not cancelled for ordinary use either.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only here
[I would say it is forbidden] because for the Most High it is disgusting
but for an ordinary person
say: things forbidden for benefit should be cancelled by a majority
so it teaches us [that they are not]
phrases.notes: He means the משנה in עבודה זרה, which says these things forbid a mixture in any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer begun in Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source is needed for a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From our משנה alone, we might think איסורי הנאה are cancelled in a majority for ordinary use
steps.terutzMaskana: The עבודה זרה משנה teaches that they are not cancelled, so both משניות are needed

steps.title: Where do we learn that רובע and נרבע are unfit for the מזבח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks for the source that רובע and נרבע may not be brought as קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רובע and נרבע: from where do we know they are forbidden for the Most High?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and asks for the source of a rule in the משנה. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed רובע and נרבע among animals that cannot go on the מזבח. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person
An animal that a person mated with
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And an animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with
from where do we know that they are forbidden for the Most High?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the mixture discussion to the source for one of the disqualified animals
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that רובע and נרבע are unfit as קרבנות

steps.title: The source is the words "from the animals"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words מן הבהמה that רובע and נרבע are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "From the animals" comes to exclude רובע and נרבע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The word "from" in the פסוק means only some animals, not all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to bring a קרבן "from the animals." The word "from" means some, not all, so certain animals are left out. The ברייתא says that רובע and נרבע are among those left out.

keyTerms.meaning: "From the animals": the words the rule is learned from
To exclude, to leave out

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught
"From the animals"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2

phrases.english: comes to exclude an animal that mated with a person and one that a person mated with

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִן הַבְּהֵמָה לְהוֹצִיא רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "from" in מן הבהמה leaves out רובע and נרבע

steps.title: Why do we need a פסוק if logic already teaches it?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: a בעל מום is unfit even though no sin was done with it. So רובע and נרבע, which a sin was done with, should surely be unfit. Why do we need a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it a logical argument? A blemished animal had no sin done with it, yet it is unfit for the מזבח. רובע and נרבע did have a sin done with them. Isn't it logical that they are forbidden for the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own source. It suggests that a קל וחומר could teach the rule without any פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument goes from the lighter case to the stronger one. A בעל מום did nothing wrong and is still unfit. So an animal involved in a sin should be unfit even more. If this works, the words מן הבהמה would not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical argument? (opens a קל וחומר)
An animal with a blemish
A sin
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.confusionAlert: This question is still part of the ברייתא. The ברייתא is testing its own source; the גמרא is not attacking it from outside.

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical argument?
If a blemished animal
which had no sin done with it
is unfit for the altar
then an animal that mated with a person, and one that a person mated with
which did have a sin done with them
isn't it logical that they are forbidden for the altar?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the פסוק quoted in Step 15 is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the words מן הבהמה to teach this rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from בעל מום seems to teach the same rule, so the פסוק would be extra

steps.title: The ox used for forbidden plowing breaks the logic
steps.stepSummary: An ox that was used to plow together with a donkey had a sin done with it, yet it may still be brought on the מזבח. So a sin done with an animal does not automatically make it unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who plows with an ox and a donkey together proves otherwise: a sin was done with the ox, and yet it is allowed on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר with a case that does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that any animal involved in a sin is unfit for the מזבח. The ox used in forbidden plowing seems to show that this is not true. The next step pushes back on this counter-example.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (otherwise): brings a case that breaks an argument
Plowing with an ox and a donkey together, which is forbidden
Allowed to be offered on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: An animal does not become unfit for the מזבח just because a sin was done with it. The ox used for forbidden plowing proves this, so the קל וחומר from בעל מום fails.

phrases.english: One who plows with an ox and a donkey will prove [otherwise]
phrases.notes: דברים 22:10

phrases.english: since a sin was done with it
and yet it is allowed for the altar
phrases.notes: The ox used in that plowing can still be brought as a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in Step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from בעל מום
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a sin done with an animal makes it unfit, but the plowing ox is a case where it does not

steps.title: Plowing with an ox and donkey carries no death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The ox-and-donkey challenge fails. That sin carries no death penalty, while the sin with רובע and נרבע does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Plowing with an ox and a donkey is not a sin punished by death. Can you compare it to רובע and נרבע, where the sin is punished by death?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the challenge from Step 17. The ox-and-donkey case is too weak to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said a sin done with an animal does not always make it unfit, because the plowing ox can still be offered. But plowing with mixed animals is a light sin with no death penalty. Bestiality carries a death penalty, so it is much more serious, and the קל וחומר from Step 16 stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: Plowing with an ox and a donkey together, which the תורה forbids
Liable to the death penalty
'What about...?' A formula used to show that two cases are not really alike

phrases.english: What about one who plows with an ox and a donkey,
where they are not liable to death,
phrases.notes: This means the person who did the sin is not put to death.

phrases.english: will you say the same about an animal that mated with a person, or one that a person mated with,
where they are liable to death?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-example brought in Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ox-and-donkey counter-example to the קל וחומר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That sin has no death penalty, so it is lighter than bestiality and cannot be compared to it

steps.title: The קל וחומר works only when there are two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The counter-example is dropped. The קל וחומר does prove the animal unfit, but only where two witnesses saw the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take back what you brought. This case, where the קל וחומר works, is where the sin was done with them in front of two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא accepts that the ox-and-donkey challenge failed. It then limits the קל וחומר to cases with two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty is only given when two witnesses testify. So the reason that made the קל וחומר work, that the sin carries death, only applies in a two-witness case. This prepares the next question about cases without two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Take back what you brought.' Your objection is withdrawn
Two witnesses, needed for a court to punish

phrases.english: Take back what you brought,
phrases.notes: This means: drop the ox-and-donkey proof, because it does not work here.

phrases.english: this is a case where a sin was done with them
in front of two witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 18 and sets the limit of the קל וחומר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קל וחומר disqualifies רובע and נרבע only when two witnesses saw the sin, because only then is there a death penalty.

steps.title: What if only one witness or the owner knows?
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר does not cover a case with only one witness or the owner's own word. So the פסוק מן הבהמה is needed for that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the sin was done with them based on one witness, or based on the owners, from where do we know the animal is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about the case the קל וחומר does not reach. This explains why the ברייתא still needs the פסוק from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one witness or the owner's word, nobody is put to death. So the 'death penalty' reason from Step 18 is missing, and the קל וחומר breaks down. That gap is the job of the פסוק, which answers the question of Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: One single witness, which is not enough for a court to punish
Based on what the owners themselves say
From where do we know?

phrases.english: If a sin was done with them
based on one witness,
or based on the owners,
phrases.notes: The owner himself says this happened with his animal.

phrases.english: from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶעֶבְדָה בָּהֶן עֲבֵירָה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the gap left by the limited קל וחומר in Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the animal is unfit when the sin is known only through one witness or the owner
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ברייתא's real answer to Step 16: the פסוק מן הבהמה is needed for the cases a קל וחומר cannot cover.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns even the one-witness case with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון builds a new קל וחומר from בעל מום. One witness is enough to make a blemished animal unfit for the מזבח, so one witness should surely be enough for רובע and נרבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: I can prove it with logic. Take a בעל מום: even if two witnesses testify about it, it is not forbidden to eat, yet one witness makes it unfit to offer. Now take רובע and נרבע, where two witnesses make it forbidden to eat. Isn't it logical that one witness should make it unfit to offer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון says we do not need the פסוק even for the one-witness case. A new קל וחומר covers it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish is the weaker problem: even when proven, it never forbids eating. Still, one person's word is enough to keep the animal off the מזבח. Bestiality is the stronger problem, since when it is proven the animal cannot even be eaten, so one person's word should surely keep it off the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I reason.' I can prove it with logic, here a קל וחומר
Literally 'warning'; here, formal testimony
Literally 'admission'; here, a statement or report
Eating / offering on the מזבח
'Is it not logical?' The closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of unfit. 'Unfit to eat' means even an ordinary person may not eat it. 'Unfit to offer' only means it cannot go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said: I reason,
if a blemished animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין הַתְרָאַת שְׁנֵי עֵדִים פּוֹסַלְתּוֹ מֵאֲכִילָה —
phrases.english: which even the testimony of two witnesses does not make forbidden to eat,
phrases.notes: A blemish never stops an ordinary person from eating the animal, however clearly it is proven.

phrases.english: the word of one witness makes it unfit to offer,
then for an animal that mated with a person, or one that a person mated with,
which the testimony of two witnesses makes forbidden to eat,
is it not logical
that the word of one witness makes it unfit to offer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 20 that the one-witness case needs a פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק מן הבהמה is needed for the one-witness or owner case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from בעל מום: a weaker problem needs only one witness to block offering, so the stronger problem of bestiality surely does too

steps.title: The verse is what rules out these animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" is what makes רובע and נרבע unfit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says "from the animals" to leave out an animal that had relations with a person (רובע) and an animal a person had relations with (נרבע).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up its argument. Logic alone did not settle the case, so it points to the פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" as the real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps showed that the first קל וחומר works only when two witnesses saw the sin. רבי שמעון then offered a second קל וחומר for the one-witness or owner case, yet the ברייתא still points to the words "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" as the source. Those words mean "some of the animals, not all," so they leave out רובע and נרבע in every case. The next step asks why the פסוק is needed if רבי שמעון's logic already works.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches." The ברייתא is pointing to a פסוק as its source
"From the animals." The word "from" means some animals, not all of them
To exclude, to leave out
An animal that had relations with a person, and an animal that a person had relations with

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" is the source that רובע and נרבע may not be brought on the מזבח.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "From the animals"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2

phrases.english: to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was used for bestiality

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא's argument by naming the פסוק as the source, after the logical arguments were tried.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" excludes רובע and נרבע from being brought as קרבנות.

steps.title: Why do we need a verse if logic already proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק is needed, since רבי שמעון's קל וחומר already taught this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this law already comes from logic! Why do we need a פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If רבי שמעון's קל וחומר already proves the law, the פסוק looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רבי שמעון reasoned that one witness is enough to disqualify a בעל מום, so one witness should surely be enough for רובע and נרבע. That covers even the one-witness case that step 20 asked about. So the reason for needing the פסוק seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: "But surely." Opens a challenge
"It comes from logic," meaning it can be learned through a קל וחומר

phrases.english: But it is derived through logical inference!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי שמעון's קל וחומר from a blemished animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22 by using רבי שמעון's קל וחומר from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" in step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק should not be needed for a law that logic already proves. רבי שמעון's קל וחומר covers even the one-witness case.

steps.title: The logic does not actually work
steps.stepSummary: Some versions have a short answer here, in round brackets: the law cannot really be learned from the קל וחומר, so the פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not come from logic.
steps.whatsHappening: Some versions have a two-word answer to the challenge: the קל וחומר does not really prove this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבי שמעון's קל וחומר is his own view. The רבנן who disagree with him do not accept it, so for them the פסוק is the source and is not extra. The challenge from step 23 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: "It does not come," meaning it cannot be learned that way

steps.confusionAlert: These two words are in round brackets. Some versions of the גמרא have them and some don't. Without them, step 23 stands as a question that the גמרא goes on to deal with.

phrases.english: (It cannot be derived that way.)
phrases.notes: These words are in round brackets, so some versions of the גמרא have them and some leave them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by denying that the קל וחומר works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that the law can be learned through logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's קל וחומר proves the law, so the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law cannot be learned from the קל וחומר, so the פסוק "מִן הַבְּהֵמָה" is needed.
